import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.11

by G. Baumslag

Let $F$ be the free group of rank $2$ in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not finitely
presented as an abstract group, is its Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ necessarily
not finitely generated as an abelian group?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

/-- A variety of small groups, expressed by the closure properties in Birkhoff's HSP theorem:
closure under isomorphisms, subgroups, quotient groups, and arbitrary direct products. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  Mem : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop
  mem_of_mulEquiv : ∀ {G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H], G ≃* H → Mem G → Mem H
  subgroup_mem : ∀ {G : Type} [Group G], Mem G → (H : Subgroup G) → Mem H
  quotient_mem : ∀ {G : Type} [Group G], Mem G → (N : Subgroup G) → [N.Normal] → Mem (G ⧸ N)
  pi_mem : ∀ {ι : Type} {G : ι → Type} [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, Mem (G i)) → Mem (∀ i, G i)

/-- A group is relatively free of rank two in `V` if it belongs to `V` and has two distinguished
free generators with the universal mapping property among groups in `V`. -/
def IsRelativelyFreeRankTwo (V : GroupVariety) (F : Type) [Group F] : Prop :=
  V.Mem F ∧ ∃ x : Fin 2 → F, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G →
    ∀ y : Fin 2 → G, ∃! φ : F →* G, ∀ i, φ (x i) = y i

/-- An abstract group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group with finitely many
numbered generators and finitely many defining relations. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

/-- The Schur multiplicator of `G`, namely the second integral homology group
$H_2(G, \mathbb{Z})$ with trivial coefficients. -/
noncomputable abbrev schurMultiplicator (G : Type) [Group G] :=
  groupHomology (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ) 2

/--
Let $F$ be the free group of rank $2$ in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not finitely
presented as an abstract group, is its Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ necessarily
not finitely generated as an abelian group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : GroupVariety) (F : Type) [Group F],
      IsRelativelyFreeRankTwo V F → ¬ IsFinitelyPresented F →
      ¬ AddGroup.FG (schurMultiplicator F) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.11»
modeling_decisions: A variety of groups is represented extensionally, using Birkhoff's HSP characterization: closure under group isomorphisms, subgroups, quotient groups, and arbitrary direct products.

Being free of rank 2 in a variety is represented by membership in the variety together with a chosen map from `Fin 2` satisfying the unique-extension universal property against every group in the variety.
Abstract finite presentation is represented by isomorphism to `PresentedGroup rels` for some `Fin n` and finite set of relators; this does not use relative presentation in the variety.
The multiplicator is modeled as Mathlib's second group homology with the trivial integral representation, `groupHomology (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ) 2`. Infinite generation is `¬ AddGroup.FG`.
The definitions quantify over small groups (`Type`), aligning the group universe with the coefficient universe required by Mathlib's current `groupHomology` API.

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

/-- A variety of groups, represented by a set of defining identities in countably many
variables. An element of `identities` is a group word that is required to equal $1$. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  identities : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)

/-- All substitution instances, in two generators, of the identities defining `V`. -/
def rankTwoRelations (V : GroupVariety) : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 2)) :=
  {r | ∃ w ∈ V.identities, ∃ f : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2), FreeGroup.lift f w = r}

/-- The relatively free group of rank $2$ in the variety `V`. -/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (V : GroupVariety) := PresentedGroup (rankTwoRelations V)

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group with finitely many
generators and finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- The multiplicator (Schur multiplier) of a presented group, expressed by Hopf's formula
$(R \cap [G,G])/[R,G]$, where $G$ is the free group and $R$ is the normal closure of the
relators. -/
abbrev multiplicator {α : Type*} (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) :=
  let R := Subgroup.normalClosure rels
  let numerator := R ⊓ commutator (FreeGroup α)
  numerator ⧸ (⁅R, (⊤ : Subgroup (FreeGroup α))⁆.subgroupOf numerator)

/--
Let $F$ be the free group of rank $2$ in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not finitely
presented as an abstract group, is its multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ necessarily not
finitely generated (as an abelian group)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety, ¬ IsFinitelyPresented (RelativelyFreeGroup V) →
      ¬ Group.FG (multiplicator (rankTwoRelations V)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.11»
modeling_decisions: A variety of groups is represented by an arbitrary set of identities in the free group on countably many variables. Every such identity set defines a variety, and every group variety admits such a presentation.
The relatively free group of rank 2 is constructed by quotienting `FreeGroup (Fin 2)` by the normal closure of every substitution instance of every defining identity.

Finite presentability is defined intrinsically up to group isomorphism by the existence of a presentation with `Fin n` generators and a finite set of relators; it is therefore abstract finite presentability, not finite presentation relative to the variety.

The multiplicator is represented using Hopf's formula `(R ∩ [G,G])/[R,G]` for the displayed free presentation. `Group.FG` is used for finite generation; on this abelian quotient it is equivalent to finite generation as an abelian group.
The phrase “necessarily” is modeled, as required by the decomposition, by universal quantification over all represented varieties inside the proposition compared with `answer(sorry)`.

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

/-- The verbal subgroup of the free group on `X` determined by a set `W` of
words in countably many variables. It is the normal closure of all values of
words in `W` under substitutions of elements of the free group for variables. -/
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) : Subgroup (FreeGroup X) :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure {x | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → FreeGroup X, FreeGroup.lift f w = x}

instance (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) : (verbalSubgroup W X).Normal := by
  unfold verbalSubgroup
  infer_instance

/-- The relatively free group on `X` in the variety defined by the group
identities `W`. Every variety of groups can be specified by such a set of words. -/
abbrev relativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) :=
  FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup W X

/-- A group is finitely presented as an abstract group if it is isomorphic to
a free group on finitely many generators modulo the normal closure of finitely
many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresentedGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (R : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup (Fin n) ⧸ Subgroup.normalClosure (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

Let $F$ be the relatively free group of rank $2$ in an arbitrary variety of
groups. If $F$ is not finitely presented as an abstract group, must its Schur
multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ be not finitely generated as an abelian group?

    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      ¬ IsFinitelyPresentedGroup (relativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)) →
        ¬ AddGroup.FG
          (groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ (relativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)) ℤ)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.11»

/-!
# Conjecture 4.11

by G. Baumslag

Let $F$ be the free group of rank 2 in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not finitely
presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying a given set $W$ of laws, where a law
is a word in the free group $F_\infty$ on countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$. By
Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups closed under subgroups, homomorphic
images and cartesian products. The free group of rank $2$ in the variety defined by $W$ is the
relatively free group $F_2 / W(F_2)$, where $F_2$ is the free group of rank $2$ and $W(F_2)$ is
its verbal subgroup determined by $W$, i.e. the subgroup generated by all values in $F_2$ of the
words in $W$.

"Finitely presented" refers to $F$ as an abstract group, not relative to the variety. The
multiplicator of $F$ is the Schur multiplicator $M(F) = H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$, which by Hopf's
formula equals $(R \cap [G, G]) / [R, G]$ for any presentation $F = G / R$ with $G$ free.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

/--
The verbal subgroup $W(G)$ of a group $G$ determined by a set $W$ of words (laws) in the free
group on countably many variables: the subgroup of $G$ generated by all values in $G$ of the words
in $W$. The set of values is closed under conjugation, so this subgroup is the normal closure of
the set of values.
-/
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = g}

instance (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure_normal

/--
The free group on the set `α` of free generators in the variety of groups defined by the set of
laws `W`: the relatively free group $F / W(F)$, where $F$ is the free group on `α` and $W(F)$ is its
verbal subgroup determined by `W`.
-/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (α : Type*) :=
  FreeGroup α ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup α)

/--
A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many generators
and finitely many defining relations.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

/-- The verbal subgroup determined by the empty set of laws is trivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_empty (G : Type*) [Group G] : verbalSubgroup ∅ G = ⊥ :=
  le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (by simp))

/-- If the law $x_0$ holds, the verbal subgroup is the whole group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_eq_top_of_mem (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (h : FreeGroup.of 0 ∈ W) : verbalSubgroup W G = ⊤ :=
  top_le_iff.mp fun g _ => Subgroup.subset_normalClosure ⟨_, h, FreeGroup.lift fun _ => g, by simp⟩

/-- The free group of rank $2$ in the variety of all groups is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_relativelyFreeGroup_empty :
    IsFinitelyPresented (RelativelyFreeGroup ∅ (Fin 2)) :=
  ⟨2, ∅, Set.finite_empty, ⟨QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq <|
    (le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _))).trans
      (verbalSubgroup_empty _).symm⟩⟩

/-- The free group of rank $2$ in the trivial variety (defined by the law $x_0$) is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem subsingleton_relativelyFreeGroup_of_mem (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (h : FreeGroup.of 0 ∈ W) :
    Subsingleton (RelativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)) := by
  rw [RelativelyFreeGroup, verbalSubgroup_eq_top_of_mem W _ h]
  exact QuotientGroup.subsingleton_quotient_top

Let $F$ be the free group of rank 2 in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not finitely
presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

The variety is given by an arbitrary set of laws `W`, and $F$ is the relatively free group
`RelativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)`. "Finitely presented" is as an abstract group. The multiplicator
of $F$ is the Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$, i.e. `groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ F ℤ)`,
and "infinitely generated" means not finitely generated as an abelian group.
-/

    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      ¬ IsFinitelyPresented (RelativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)) →
      ¬ AddGroup.FG (groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ (RelativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)) ℤ)) := by
  sorry

by G. Baumslag

Let $F$ be the free group of rank $2$ in a variety of groups. If $F$ is not finitely
presented as an abstract group, is its Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ necessarily
not finitely generated?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

/-- A variety of groups, specified by the group words in countably many variables that are
identically equal to $1$. -/
abbrev GroupVariety := Set (FreeGroup ℕ)

/-- A group satisfies a variety if each defining word evaluates to $1$ under every substitution
of its variables by elements of the group. -/
def Satisfies {G : Type} [Group G] (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ V, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- The map `ι` exhibits `F` as the relatively free group on two generators in the variety `V`.
That is, `F` satisfies the identities of `V`, and every map from its two distinguished generators
to a group satisfying `V` extends uniquely to a group homomorphism. -/
def IsRelativelyFreeOnTwo {F : Type} [Group F] (V : GroupVariety) (ι : Fin 2 → F) : Prop :=
  Satisfies V (G := F) ∧
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Satisfies V (G := G) → ∀ f : Fin 2 → G,
      ∃! φ : F →* G, ∀ i, φ (ι i) = f i

/-- A group is finitely presented as an abstract group if it is isomorphic to a group with
finitely many generators and finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

/--
Let $F$ be the free group of rank $2$ in an arbitrary variety of groups. If $F$ is not finitely
presented as an abstract group, is its Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ necessarily not
finitely generated as an abelian group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : GroupVariety) (F : Type) [Group F] (ι : Fin 2 → F),
      IsRelativelyFreeOnTwo V ι → ¬IsFinitelyPresented F →
        ¬AddGroup.FG (groupHomology (Rep.trivial ℤ F ℤ) 2) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.11»

finitely presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying a given set $W$ of laws,
where a law is a word $w$ in the free group on the countably many variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$, and a group $G$ satisfies $w$ if every substitution of elements
of $G$ for the variables sends $w$ to $1$. The free group of rank 2 in this variety
is $F_2 / W(F_2)$, where $F_2$ is the absolutely free group on two generators and
$W(F_2)$ is its verbal subgroup, i.e. the subgroup generated by all values of the
words of $W$ in $F_2$.

"Finitely presented" is meant as an abstract group. The multiplicator of $F$ is
its Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ (the second integral homology group
of $F$ with trivial coefficients); by Hopf's formula it is isomorphic to
$(R \cap [G, G]) / [R, G]$ for any presentation $F = G / R$ with $G$ free.
"Infinitely generated" means not finitely generated as an abelian group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

variable (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- The verbal subgroup $W(G)$ of a group $G$ determined by a set $W$ of laws (words in the
free group on the countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$): the subgroup generated by all
values $\varphi(w)$, for $w \in W$ and $\varphi : F_\infty \to G$ a homomorphism (i.e. a
substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables). -/
def verbalSubgroup : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ (w : FreeGroup ℕ) (φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G), w ∈ W ∧ φ w = g}

/-- A verbal subgroup is normal: conjugating a value of a law gives another value of the
same law. -/
instance verbalSubgroup_normal : (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := by
    have h : (verbalSubgroup W G).map (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom ≤ verbalSubgroup W G := by
      rw [verbalSubgroup, MonoidHom.map_closure]
      refine Subgroup.closure_mono ?_
      rintro _ ⟨_, ⟨w, φ, hw, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨w, (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom.comp φ, hw, rfl⟩
    exact h ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩

/-- The free group on the generating set `α` in the variety of groups defined by the set of
laws `W`, namely the quotient of the (absolutely) free group on `α` by its verbal subgroup. -/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (α : Type*) :=
  FreeGroup α ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup α)

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- The verbal subgroup determined by the empty set of laws (the variety of all groups) is
trivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_empty : verbalSubgroup ∅ G = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- The verbal subgroup determined by the law $x_0$ (the variety of trivial groups) is
the whole group. -/

theorem verbalSubgroup_of_zero : verbalSubgroup {FreeGroup.of 0} G = ⊤ := by
  rw [eq_top_iff]
  rintro g -
  refine Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.lift (fun _ => g), rfl, ?_⟩
  simp

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and finitely many relators is finitely
presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))

  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

finitely presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

Formally: for every set of laws $W$ (i.e. every variety of groups), if the free

generated abelian group. Here $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$ is `groupHomology` of the trivial
$F$-representation on $\mathbb{Z}$ in degree $2$, and finite generation of an abelian group
is `Module.Finite ℤ`.
-/

    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      ¬ IsFinitelyPresented (RelativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)) →
      ¬ Module.Finite ℤ (groupHomology (Rep.trivial ℤ (RelativelyFreeGroup W (Fin 2)) ℤ) 2) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.11»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.11

by G. Baumslag

Let $F$ be the free group of rank 2 in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not
finitely presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying a given set $W$ of
laws. A law is a word $w$ in the free group $F_\infty$ on the countably many
variables $x_0, x_1, \ldots$, and a group $G$ satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates
to $1$ under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables. The free
group of rank $2$ in the variety defined by $W$ is the relatively free group
$F_2 / W(F_2)$, where $F_2$ is the (absolutely) free group of rank $2$ and
$W(F_2)$ is its verbal subgroup, the subgroup generated by all values of the
words $w \in W$ on $F_2$. Every variety of groups arises from some set of laws
$W$, so quantifying over all $W$ quantifies over all varieties.

The multiplicator of a group $F$ is its Schur multiplicator, the second
integral homology group $M(F) = H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$. By Hopf's formula this is
$(R \cap [G, G]) / [R, G]$ for any presentation $F = G / R$ with $G$ free.

"Finitely presented" refers to $F$ as an abstract group (finitely many
generators and finitely many relators), not to presentations relative to the
variety. "Infinitely generated" means not finitely generated as an abelian
group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w`, a word in the free group on the countably many variables
`x₀, x₁, …`, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the
variables. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- The verbal subgroup `W(G)` of a group `G` determined by a set `W` of laws: the subgroup
generated by all values `w(g₀, g₁, …)` of the words `w ∈ W` on `G`. -/
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = g}

/-- Conjugating the value of a word gives the value of the word at the conjugated
substitution. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma conj_lift {G : Type*} [Group G] (f : ℕ → G) (c : G) (w : FreeGroup ℕ) :
    c * FreeGroup.lift f w * c⁻¹ = FreeGroup.lift (fun i => c * f i * c⁻¹) w :=
  FreeGroup.lift_unique ((MulAut.conj c).toMonoidHom.comp (FreeGroup.lift f)) (fun x => by simp)

/-- The set of values of the words in `W` is closed under conjugation, so the verbal subgroup
`W(G)` is normal. -/
instance verbalSubgroup_normal (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal := by
  refine ⟨fun n hn c => ?_⟩
  refine Subgroup.closure_induction (fun x hx => ?_) ?_ (fun x y _ _ ihx ihy => ?_)
    (fun x _ ihx => ?_) hn
  · obtain ⟨w, hw, f, rfl⟩ := hx
    exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, fun i => c * f i * c⁻¹, (conj_lift f c w).symm⟩
  · simp
  · rw [← conj_mul]
    exact mul_mem ihx ihy
  · rw [← conj_inv]
    exact inv_mem ihx

/-- The verbal subgroup for the empty set of laws (the variety of all groups) is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma verbalSubgroup_empty (G : Type*) [Group G] : verbalSubgroup ∅ G = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- The free group of rank `n` in the variety of groups defined by the set of laws `W`, i.e.
the relatively free group `Fₙ / W(Fₙ)`, the quotient of the (absolutely) free group `Fₙ` of
rank `n` by its verbal subgroup. -/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (n : ℕ) : Type :=
  FreeGroup (Fin n) ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup (Fin n))

/-- The free group of rank `n` in the variety defined by `W` satisfies every law in `W`, i.e.
it belongs to the variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma satisfiesLaw_relativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (n : ℕ) {w : FreeGroup ℕ}
    (hw : w ∈ W) : SatisfiesLaw (RelativelyFreeGroup W n) w := by
  intro f
  choose f' hf' using fun i => QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (f i)
  have : FreeGroup.lift f =
      (QuotientGroup.mk' (verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup (Fin n)))).comp (FreeGroup.lift f') := by
    ext i
    simp [hf']
  rw [this, MonoidHom.comp_apply, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, f', rfl⟩

/-- A group `G` is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relators. -/
def FinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma FinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : FinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) := Group.fg_iff.2
    ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

/-- A free group of finite rank is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma finitelyPresented_freeGroup (n : ℕ) : FinitelyPresented (FreeGroup (Fin n)) := by
  refine ⟨n, ∅, Set.finite_empty, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  have h : Subgroup.normalClosure (∅ : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) = ⊥ :=
    le_bot_iff.1 (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _))
  exact ((QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq h).trans QuotientGroup.quotientBot).symm

/-- The Schur multiplicator `M(G) = H₂(G, ℤ)` of a group `G`: its second homology group with
trivial integral coefficients. -/
noncomputable abbrev schurMultiplicator (G : Type) [Group G] : ModuleCat ℤ :=
  groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ)

/--
Let $F$ be the free group of rank 2 in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not
finitely presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

Here the variety is the one defined by an arbitrary set $W$ of laws, $F = F_2 / W(F_2)$
is its free group of rank $2$, "finitely presented" refers to $F$ as an abstract group,
and the multiplicator of $F$ is the Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$, which is
"infinitely generated" if it is not finitely generated as an abelian group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      ¬ FinitelyPresented (RelativelyFreeGroup W 2) →
        ¬ AddGroup.FG (schurMultiplicator (RelativelyFreeGroup W 2)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.11»

modeling_decisions: Varieties of groups are modelled by arbitrary sets of laws W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ) (words in countably many variables x₀, x₁, …); by definition (and Birkhoff's theorem for the HSP formulation) every variety is defined by some such W, so ∀ W ranges over all varieties. Different W may define the same variety, which is harmless for a universal statement.

The free group of rank 2 in the variety defined by W is taken to be F₂/W(F₂) (quotient of FreeGroup (Fin 2) by the verbal subgroup), the standard construction of relatively free groups; the verbal subgroup is defined as Subgroup.closure of the set of word values, with normality proved.

'Finitely presented' is formalized as an abstract-group property: isomorphic to PresentedGroup rels for a finite type Fin n of generators and a finite set of relators (the notebook's intended meaning per the decomposition notes, not finite presentability within the variety).

The multiplicator is the Schur multiplicator H₂(F, ℤ), taken directly from Mathlib's `groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ F ℤ)` (inhomogeneous chains, trivial integral coefficients), rather than via Hopf's formula; the docstring records Hopf's formula for orientation only.
'Infinitely generated' is formalized as `¬ AddGroup.FG` of the carrier of the ModuleCat ℤ object; this is equivalent to `¬ Module.Finite ℤ` (checked via Module.Finite.iff_addGroup_fg).

Positive answer: answer(True) ⇔ for every variety, non-finitely-presented relatively free group of rank 2 has non-finitely-generated multiplicator. Degenerate varieties (trivial variety, variety of all groups, finite relatively free groups) give finitely presented F and are excluded by the hypothesis, matching the source.
Universe: F lives in Type (as required by `Rep ℤ F` with ℤ : Type); this is no restriction since F₂/W(F₂) is a Type-level object.
